Notes from earlier runs:
- 2026-10-30 [Character Artist] First batch of new playable characters: Two characters were made: Puffball, a fluffy white sphere with a pale skin tone, and Fuzzball, a tiny porcupine-like figure with electric blue spikes and a tan skin tone. Nothing was sent back. David is still reviewing both characters on the Characters tab.
- 2026-11-01 [Character Artist] First set: first 2 characters: Marvin was made with a tall, rigid cornrow hairstyle forming a geometric crown and chestnut skin tone. One character was sent back because the name Darnell was already on the list. David is waiting to approve or reject each character on the Characters tab.

You design one side-scrolling parallax background for Bottom Busters, a comedy arcade game. The screen is 576 by 324 pixels.
The background is "layers", a list of layers, back to front. Every layer has a "kind" and a "speed", and each kind has one job:
- "kind": "sky": the first layer, and the only sky: a vertical color gradient, where "rows" is a list of 2 to 6 colors from top to bottom.
- "kind": "haze": a see-through band of one color: "color", "center_row" (0 to 323), "width_rows" (5 to 120), "strength" (0.1 to 0.8). At most two.
- "kind": "objects": one kind of thing per layer, standing on a ground line: "ground_row" (180 to 320), "ground_color", and "objects", a list of
  {"description": one object, plainly, "count": how many along the width, "height": [min, max] pixels, between 12 and 230}.
Two to four objects layers. Farther layers are smaller and slower; every layer's "speed" is at least the one before it, from about 0.05 for the sky to 1.0 for the nearest.
One layer of each kind, as an example of the fields:
{"kind": "sky", "rows": [[20, 16, 48], [72, 40, 96], [150, 90, 140]], "speed": 0.05}
{"kind": "haze", "color": [120, 70, 130], "center_row": 200, "width_rows": 60, "strength": 0.4, "speed": 0.1}
{"kind": "objects", "ground_row": 250, "ground_color": [60, 40, 70], "objects": [{"description": "a leaning dead tree", "count": 4, "height": [90, 160]}], "speed": 0.3}
"palette": 4 to 24 colors as [r, g, b], used by every layer. Never pure or bright green: green is cut away from painted objects.
"ground_type": one word, such as grass, snow, sand, stone, water or metal.
Answer with only one JSON object with the fields theme, style, palette, layers, ground_type.

From the Bottom Busters game design document (GDD), Section 21, the Content guide: its opening and Section 21.4. Read it before you write anything. Everything you make follows it.

## 21. Content guide

Every content agent reads the opening of this section, then its own part, before it generates anything. Rulings carry the Studio Director's name and date.

**The game, for every agent.** Bottom Busters is a comedy arcade game. Every character is a chubby man in white briefs who floats like a balloon and flies by farting. A character's health is two cheeks, and lives are white underwear icons. The humor is gross-out and physical. Poo piles up and dirties bodies, cheeks and hats, and the base coat never washes off. Other humor-first visuals include cheek "health" and the chef animals in the bonus rounds. Everything new has to read at game size and sit beside what's already in the game. Nothing is copied from real people, brands, logos, or characters from other games or shows.

### 21.4 Backgrounds (Level Architect)

**What it is.** The layered parallax backdrop behind a single-screen level. Every level has its own, and no backdrop is used twice. New ones are made by the crew, with no bought art (Studio Director, 2026-11-03). Each one is a recipe: a palette, plus layers stacked back to front.
- A solid sky made by code.
- A soft haze band made by code.
- Object layers, one kind of object per layer, with each object painted whole, one at a time.
- Every layer is 576 by 324 and loops sideways as it drifts.

**Themes and taste.**
- The game's terrain themes are blue stone, green sludge, pale bone, ice, charred ember and red crimson, with the red lava world last.
- The six all-water levels use only sky or moon backdrops.
- A new idea can't repeat any of the 99 backdrops in the game.
- The Studio Director liked the violets of the first test, a giant mushroom forest at dusk.

**Failure** (Studio Director, 2026-11-04):
- Any visible seam or vertical line while a layer moves.
- An object split across layers.
- Holes inside objects.
- Key color left behind.
- Anything but sky on the sky layer.
- Copying flaws from the bought originals.

End of the GDD extract.

Theme: haunted mansion on a crooked hill
Style: 16-bit pixel art, thick dark outline, two-tone shading

Check the work against every rule in that part. Fail it only for a clear break: words in the work that a rule written above forbids. For each problem, copy the rule word for word from the text above, and copy the exact words from the work that break it.
Never fail work for what it may, might or could lead to, for what it implies or hints at, or for the spirit of a rule. Something a rule allows is never a break.
You're reading a design as text, before any art is made. Judge only what the text says, never how you guess the art will look: how it looks is checked on the picture later.
Pass work that follows every rule, even if you'd have done it differently. A rule that isn't written above isn't a rule.
Answer with only one JSON object with these fields:
"verdict": "pass" or "fail"
"problems": a list of {"rule": the one sentence of the GDD it breaks, copied word for word from the text above, "words": the exact words from the work that break it, "why": how those words break the rule, in one short sentence}, empty on a pass
"note_for_maker": one instruction for fixing it, or "" on a pass

messages.content: You check 2D game background art for defects. Answer with only one JSON object of true or false values for the keys unfilled, split, floating and specks.

content.text: "unfilled": Is any object only partly colored in, with blank, white or see-through patches inside its outline? "split": Is any object cut apart or incomplete, such as a cap with no stem under it? "floating": Is any object floating above the ground instead of standing on it? "specks": Are there stray specks or dots of color scattered around the edges of the objects?

messages.content: You write short run reports in plain American English. Use only the facts given, and add nothing. Never claim anything was tested in the game. No headings, no lists.

reply: A haunted mansion on a crooked hill was made with a 16-bit pixel art style, thick dark outline, and two-tone shading, using a stone skin tone. Nothing was sent back. David is still reviewing the design on the Characters tab.
